context: frozen exhaustive OR-pair v2 macro semantics

definitions.p: number of clauses containing +x before the macro
definitions.q: number of clauses containing -x before the macro
definitions.t: number of clauses containing both +x and b

lemma.statement: Apply the frozen v2 macro to the pair (+x,b). Before canonical duplicate/subsumption deletion, the resulting macro CNF has exactly p-t+1 clauses containing +x and q+1 clauses containing -x. Therefore after canonicalization its positive and negative x-parent counts p',q' satisfy p'<=p-t+1 and q'<=q+1, hence p'q' <= (p-t+1)(q+1).
proof: Exactly the t clauses containing both +x and b are replaced by clauses containing -e and the old remainder, so those t clauses no longer contain x.
All other old +x clauses are untouched, giving p-t surviving positive x parents before canonical cleanup.
The definition clause (e,x,b) adds one positive x parent.
The definition clause (-e,-x) adds one negative x parent, while (-e,-b) contains no x.
Thus pre-canonical parent counts are p-t+1 and q+1 exactly.
Canonicalization can delete duplicate/subsumed clauses but cannot create additional x parents, giving the stated inequalities.

corollary.statement: The raw Cartesian parent-pair count decreases by at least D_pair = p*q-(p-t+1)(q+1) = t*(q+1)-(p+q+1), whenever this quantity is positive.
corollary.symmetric_case: For a pair (-x,b), exchange p and q.
